rv.q: All the very talented people involved would probably get a decent grade for this scene study in theater school, but it’s not a vessel fit for paying customers.

Director Thomas Kail—best known for large-scale Broadway musicals such as Hamilton and the recent Sweeney Todd—doesn’t seem to have a fully formed vision for the production. (Perhaps it’s lost in the fog. Seriously…enough with the dry ice.) What he does have is a wonderful showcase for his wife, Wil...

More problematically, Williams doesn’t bring the necessary intensity to the role of a young, hard-edged prostitute who falls in love with Mat Burke (Tom Sturridge), a shipwrecked Irish stoker who literally emerges from the sea. In her opening scene, when she walks into a waterfront saloon and utters...
While the play’s title is “Anna Christie” it could easily be called “Christopher Christopherson” because in this production it is Brian d’Arcy James who is at the helm.

An intoxicatingly atmospheric production and committed performance from Michelle Williams can’t disguise that Anna Christie‘s version of female empowerment involves forgiving everyone who wronged you.
Anna Christie remains a curiosity — but one that deserves a warmer, more thoughtful embrace than it gets here.
